title: How to put 170 atoms in an atom
summary: The article explains how scientists can fit multiple atoms inside a single atom by creating a Rydberg atom—a highly excited atom with an outermost electron orbiting at a much larger radius than usual. By cooling additional atoms to near absolute zero using a Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC), these atoms can be trapped within the Rydberg atom's expanded orbital, forming a Rydberg polaron. This exotic quantum structure allows up to 170 atoms to coexist within another atom without violating physical laws, offering insights into quantum mechanics and atomic behavior.
key_points: Atoms are mostly empty space, with the nucleus being tens of thousands of times smaller than the electron's orbital radius.
Rydberg atoms are created by exciting an electron to a higher energy level, expanding the atom's size up to 1000 times larger than normal.
A Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) is used to cool atoms to near absolute zero, reducing their energy and allowing them to be packed closely together.
In 2018, scientists created a Rydberg polaron by exciting a strontium atom in a BEC, trapping up to 170 additional atoms within its expanded orbital.
Rydberg polarons provide valuable insights into quantum mechanics and atomic interactions, though their practical applications are not yet clear.
